criteria.note:
Gallery:
- Seven real slides; one touch swipe moves exactly one slide (2 / 7) and loads that slide and its neighbour.
- A vertical drag that starts on the photo scrolls the page (scrollY 295).
- Each slide is a named group ('1 of 7, worn on the wrist'), and a polite region announces the position after a swipe.
- The ruler stays 320 px wide at 320, so its labels are 11 px.
- Tapping a photo opens the viewer with the 896x1200 original, and Back closes it with focus returned.

Remaining:
(1) The full-screen viewer cannot be paged from the keyboard. ArrowRight leaves it on 1 / 7, Tab cycles only Close, and axe reports scrollable-region-focusable on #vtrack (vax.js). A keyboard or switch user who presses Enter on the gallery is stuck on one photo (fix 6).
(2) 'Size guide' in the specs scrolls the page 1,953 px to the top to show slide 6 (fix 3).
(3) Still waiting on inputs: no zoom of its own (visualViewport.scale stays 1 on a double tap), and a 720w hero that is a 1.5x upscale on DPR 3.

No MP4 bytes load before a tap, and the tap makes one 142 KB request. 'Creator collaboration · Riya' shows in the viewer, and the clip plays once with sound, then loops muted. Both tiles and the chip name the clip by their content. The source is 270x480 drawn at 360x640, so it is soft; only new footage fixes that (roadmap).

What holds:
- axe-core (wcag2a/aa, 21aa, 22aa, best-practice) finds 0 violations on load, with the card open and in the one-piece bag.
- The computed-contrast scan finds no failure in any of those states; the lowest ratio is 4.84:1 (deep sage at 12 px).
- Every target in the header, page, bar, card, bag and footer is at least 44 px, and nothing is under 11 px.
- One H1 and ordered H2s. The fold headings are exposed as level-2 headings inside their disclosure buttons (ax.js).
- lang en-IN and a polite status region outside main.
- header, main and footer are inert under the overlays.
- Tab is trapped in the bag and viewer, and focus returns to the opener.

Round 4's WCAG 2.4.11 finding is fixed: 0 of 31 tab stops land behind the bar or the header (interact.json focusObscured []). Text spacing keeps the fact line 11 px clear.

Remaining:
(1) WCAG 2.1.1: the viewer has no keyboard paging, and its scroller is not focusable (axe scrollable-region-focusable).
(2) 'Size guide' leaves focus on the button 1,953 px below the slide it changed. A screen-reader user hears '6 of 7' with no context.
(3) At 150% and 200% text the bar labels overflow their fixed 48 px buttons: 'Add to bag' is 51/48 px tall at 150%, and 155/133 px wide by 60/48 tall at 200% (big.js, big_sheet.jpg).

What holds:
- A buy control is on screen at every scroll position.
- The folds open in place (the summary stays at 300 before and after).
- Back closes the bag, the viewer and the hand-off, keeping the scroll (1500, 900 and 2300 all return to the same y).
- The page is 3,397 px to the footer, 6.0 swipes of 563 px. Sections start at: the set 872, Up close 1548, Riya 2401, Reviews 2788, folds 2984.
- Nothing needed to decide is only inside a fold.

Worse than round 4:
(1) history.scrollRestoration = 'manual' (L983) is global. A shopper who taps the ring's or necklace's thumbnail (a real link) and comes Back lands at scrollY 0 instead of 739, the set (back.js, with and without bfcache). Round 4 set it to stop Back cancelling the bag's policy jump. Fix 2 keeps that and restores the set.

New finding: three scripted jumps own no history entry, so Android Back after them leaves the PDP (jumps.js, pol.js):
- 'Size guide' throws her from the specs at 1953 to the top;
- 'Read the policy' from 300 to 2881;
- the bag's policy line and the card's 'See the whole set' jump the same way.
In the Instagram app, Back from those positions returns her to the ad.

Lab, 150 ms RTT, 1.6 Mbps, 4x CPU, 360x640, Android fallback faces (perf.json):
- LCP on worn-720.jpg: 1.23 / 1.26 s at DPR 2 and 1.22 s at DPR 3.
- FCP 0.36-0.42 s, CLS 0.0001-0.0002.
- Before scroll: 5 image requests, 155 KB of images, 334 KB in all.
- Fonts are 71 KB and land at 2.2-2.3 s. No video bytes load.
- A Riya landing reaches LCP at 0.87 s, and a dpa landing at 1.27 s.
Every 10/10 threshold still holds.

LCP drifted about 0.1 s from round 4 (1.11-1.13 s). The cause is not a page fault: the uncompressed document grew to 107 KB (the notes panel and the inline chip) and now ends at 1128 ms, beside the 73 KB hero (214-1173 ms). In the live build, brotli, a vector logo and no notes remove most of that.

What still slows LCP:
- the JPEG hero (53 KB as WebP, 47 KB as AVIF from the same pixels, round 4);
- logo.png (18 KB, 340-783 ms).

After LCP, macro-720 (54 KB) and set-3 are released at 1227 ms and share the pipe with the fonts (1648-2253 ms). Holding them until the fonts land moves the swap earlier: 2.15 s against 2.43 / 2.20 s (perf_font.json, fix 8). These are lab figures on a static file; field data is in the roadmap.

fixes.where: CSS .above, L99. Live: the same column in JewelDetail, and the first-screen budget test.
fixes.change:
Replace both 'height:' declarations on .above with 'min-height:':
.above { display: flex; flex-direction: column; min-height: calc(100vh - var(--hdr) - var(--bar) - var(--safe) - 13px); min-height: calc(100svh - var(--hdr) - var(--bar) - var(--safe) - 13px); }
Keep .above .gal { flex: 1 1 0; min-height: 180px; max-height: min(125vw, 520px); } as it is. The photo still takes the free height up to its cap. When the facts plus the 180 px floor are taller than the screen, the column grows instead of overflowing, so the facts never paint over 'Questions before you buy?'.

Measured on variant_all5:
- the first screen is md5-identical at 360x640, 320x568, 412x732 and 360x560;
- the overlap is 0 in every case that overlapped (360x560, 320x568 and 360x600 at 130%, and 640x360, 732x412 and 844x390).

In the live budget test, add 360x560 at font scale 1.15 and 640x360. Assert that #product-facts' bottom is at or above the next section's top, as well as the existing check that the delivery line ends above the bar.
fixes.why: C2 fail condition (text over text), introduced by round 4's fixed-height column. Evidence: out/overlap_compare.jpg, out/ovf_sheet.jpg, ovf.js and matrix.js.

fixes.where: L983 (history.scrollRestoration = 'manual'), openLayer() L1000-1005 and the popstate handler L1007-1013.
fixes.why: C15. The set rows' thumbnails are real links to the ring and necklace pages, and coming back to the top of the page loses her place in the set. This is a regression from round 4.

fixes.where: #tosize handler L977, vfill() L961-971, #topolicy handler L1034, the bag's data-pol branch L909, the card's data-toset branch L814.
fixes.why: C15 and C14. In the Instagram app Android Back after a jump returns to the ad, so a shopper checking fit or the policy loses the PDP. Evidence: out/size_compare.jpg, jumps.js, pol.js.

fixes.where: CSS after .above .facts (L101), and a small inline script right after div#product-facts (before div#bar, L463). Live: PdpBuyFacts.
fixes.why: C1: COD must stay above the bar for an Android 'Large' font on a 360x560 in-app viewport. Whether Instagram pins textZoom is unverified (roadmap).

fixes.change:
Let the dock test the facts as well as the controls. Change the selector to $$('#product-facts, main a, main button, main summary, footer a').
In the nf_card_shown 'under' mapping, add under.id === 'product-facts' ? 'facts' : … before the set test.
The dock then never sits over the price, ladder or delivery line. Where it would, there is no card, and the bar's '✓ Added to bag', the badge and the live region confirm the add, as they already do over the set.

Measured (docksweep.js): at 130% after a 60 px scroll the dock no longer covers '…COD available'. Every default-size add from 0 to 400 px gives the same mode as before.
fixes.why: C20: the card must never cover the price, ladder or delivery line. Evidence: out/cs2_prototype_360x640_1.3_60.png.

fixes.where: Viewer markup L572 and the document keydown handler L1019-1029
fixes.change:
Make the viewer pageable from the keyboard. - Markup:
- In keydown, after the Escape line: if (layer === 'viewer' && (ev.key === 'ArrowRight' || ev.key === 'ArrowLeft')) { ev.preventDefault(); var vk = Math.max(0, Math.min(N - 1, vIdx + (ev.key === 'ArrowRight' ? 1 : -1))); vfill(vk); vtrack.scrollTo({ left: vk * vtrack.clientWidth, behavior: smooth() }); live.textContent = (vk + 1) + ' of ' + N; } #live sits outside main, so it is not inert and still speaks. Measured (vax.js): ArrowRight moves 1 / 7 to 2 / 7, and axe on the open viewer goes from scrollable-region-focusable to 0 violations.
fixes.why: C14 (WCAG 2.1.1) and C12: Enter on the gallery opens a viewer that a keyboard or switch user cannot leave photo 1 in.

fixes.where: .btn L175, and the bar's height token --bar L64
fixes.change:
Let the bar grow with very large text instead of clipping its labels.
- .btn { height: auto; min-height: 48px; }
- After render(): new ResizeObserver(function () { document.documentElement.style.setProperty('--bar', Math.ceil(addBtn.offsetHeight + 17) + 'px'); }).observe(addBtn); (8 + 8 padding + 1 border).
.above, the footer padding, the dock and scroll-padding then follow the real bar.
At the default size the button stays 48 px and --bar stays 65 px. Not built into the variant.
fixes.why: C14: at 150% 'Add to bag · ₹2,399' is 51 px tall in a 48 px box; at 200% it is 155 px wide in 133 px and the label is cut ('DD TO BA') (out/big_sheet.jpg, big.js).
C16 and C2: a shorter window on the fallback face (from about 2.2-2.4 s to about 2.15 s, two lab runs).

fixes.where: .sl.worn (CSS L111) and the head script's landing preload L32-40. Live: JewelDetail's landing frame.
fixes.change:
Give the landing frame a placeholder of its own pixels: an 18x20 JPEG of worn-720 (758 bytes, about 1 KB inline as base64) as the slide's background-image, with background-size: cover and the same object-position. From the first paint the frame shows the whole photo, soft, rather than a band of skin over ivory.
In the live SPA, use the Shopify CDN URL at width=24, or the frame's average colour as the slide background, for whichever frame the ad map picks.
fixes.why: C2 and C16 perceived load: from 471 to 1229 ms the hero area is a top band over ivory (out/load_strip.jpg). LCP is unaffected.

keep: The first-screen column at the design target. The fact line is 13 px clear at 360x640, 360x600, 360x560, 320x568, 390x664, 412x732 and 412x846; with insets of 24, 34 and 48 px; with Android fallback faces; and at 115% and 130% on 360x640. Nothing is half-cut on tall screens, and no page scrolls sideways even at 200%.
html scroll-padding: 0 of 31 tab stops are obscured by the header or the bar, and fragment jumps land clear of the header.
The chip and its inline thumbnail in the first paint (471 ms). The bar is labelled from the first text paint.

Gallery semantics: the carousel region, named slide groups, a position announcement only after a swipe, and arrows only for keyboard users. Swipe behaviour: one slide per swipe with snap-stop, and vertical drags pass to the page.
Overlays own one history entry each. inert is set behind them, Tab is trapped inside, focus returns to the opener on close, and the 700 ms tap guards are kept on Add to bag and on the bag's checkout.
The after-add card's fit ladder (full, compact, no suggestion, mini, dock or none), measured against the photo and the controls. It has no timer and never reaches the H1.
The bag's fixed foot: the saving line and '₹X paid online · ₹Y with COD (₹Z fee)' stay in view above Secure checkout with 1-4 pieces, at 320x568, 360x640 and 390x844, and with insets of 24 and 34 px.

The loading strategy. Only the landing frame is preloaded, at high priority; the slides use data-src with an idle neighbour; the rest is released after the hero; and no video bytes load before a tap. Lab: LCP 1.22-1.27 s, a Riya landing at 0.87 s, CLS 0.0001-0.0002, and 5 image requests (155 KB) before scroll.
44 px targets everywhere and AA contrast in every state (lowest 4.84:1). axe is clean on load, with the card open and in the bag. One H1, ordered H2s, and fold headings exposed as headings.
A 3,397 px page (6.0 swipes): the set, Up close with specs, Riya, reviews, then three folds that open in place and hold nothing needed to decide.
roadmap: A real-device pass inside the Instagram app on a 360-wide Android at Font size Default, Large and Largest, on a 360x640-dp phone (about 560 px of viewport) and a taller one. Record whether Instagram pins WebView textZoom to 100, the visible viewport height, env(safe-area-inset-bottom) and when the fonts land. Fixes 1 and 4 matter only if textZoom is not pinned.

Field RUM from the Instagram webview (web-vitals LCP, INP, CLS), tagged with the in-app browser, DPR, inset and a measured text scale (Clarity tag nf_text_scale). It replaces the lab figures in C16 and sizes the large-text cases in C1 and C2.
Shopify originals at 1,440 px or wider for every gallery frame. That gives the viewer a real zoom (double tap to 2.5x, then pan) and a sharp hero on DPR 3 (C12, 10 with input).
A clip of at least 540x960, ideally the 6-10 s macro turn and an on-wrist clip under 1 MB each, to replace the 270x480 source (C13).

Port to the live SPA: the min-height column, tight mode and history entries for scripted jumps in JewelDetail. Add a sitewide rule that scroll restoration is never globally manual. Extend the first-screen budget test with 360x560 at 1.15, 640x360 landscape and a no-overlap assertion; serve the landing frame as WebP or AVIF from the CDN; ship brotli and keep the notes panel out.

Clarity after launch: nf_size and nf_bag_policy followed by a pagehide within 5 s (Back leaving the page after a jump), plus dead and rage taps on the gallery, the viewer and the dock. These confirm fixes 2 and 3 in the field.
